name: Thomas W. Gordon
role: Manager of the Boston clothing, boot and shoe house in Medora
bio: Thomas W. Gordon opened the Boston clothing house in Medora in May 1885, and the paper praised him as an enterprising merchant and a supporter of the Cow Boy. In July 1885 the store moved to a new building next to Paddock's livery stable, and through 1885 he advertised new stock of shoes, suits, hosiery, quilts and blankets. In August 1885 he led the funeral services for J. A. Freeze's two-year-old daughter and spoke at the burial of J. D. Garver's infant son. He appeared on the Billings County ticket in the spring 1886 election, began selling out at cost in May 1886, and that August announced that his address would be Glendive.
